Quarter-square table for multiply_8x8 ($1514), built at run time by build_square_tables ($14BA) on every joust_restart, over the default text screen: $0400+n the low byte of floor(n*n/4) for n = 0-255, $0500+n for n = 256-511, $0600/$0700 the matching high bytes (all 512 values checked in the play snapshot). No byte of it is loaded.
Quarter-square low bytes continued (n = $58 on); an automatic symbol here comes from an indexed read.
Quarter-square low bytes for n = 256-511, written at $14DC.
Quarter-square low bytes continued (n = $194 on).
Quarter-square high bytes for n = 0-255, written at $14CE.
Quarter-square high bytes for n = 256-511, written at $14E3; the last, n = 511, is $FF.

Load stub, copied here by the resident event manager from its template at $F925 ($FA58) and patched per event: for the Pool Joust it loads file $14 (JSR load_file $F230 with X/Y = $0820), sets CIA 1 port A as outputs and port B as inputs, drives $7F on port A (keyboard row 7 only) and jumps to $0820, joust_entry. Ran before the snapshot; nothing in the joust calls it again.
$081C-$081F (AD 00 00 00): past the stub's JMP; the template's 29th byte ($AD) and zeros, never executed or read by the joust.

POOL JOUST ENTRY, file $14's first byte (the event manager's load stub jumps here, $F93F/$F940 = $0820). As loaded it is JMP $0826, the one-time start-up; $083A-$0844 then overwrite these three bytes with NOPs ($EA), so every later jump to $0820 (PRACTICE AGAIN re-enters through reenter_event $F93E without loading) falls through to JMP $0845, the per-joust set-up.
Second byte of joust_entry's JMP: overwritten with $EA at $083F (STA $0821) during the start-up, as are $0820 and $0822.
Third byte of joust_entry's JMP, the last of the three overwritten with NOPs (STA $0822 at $0842).
JMP joust_restart ($0845): reached through the NOPs at $0820-$0822 once the start-up has run, and directly by the first pass when $0842 has finished.

One-time start-up, run once per load: $01 = $25 (RAM at $A000-$BFFF and $E000-$FFFF, I/O visible), load the font (file $15 to $6800, load_font $1408), load and unpack the two pictures (load_pictures $08A1), load the sprite files $18, $19 and $1A (load_sprite_files $0958), blank the screen (blank_screen $1D3D), clear $35 (no opponent chosen yet) and write $EA over $0820-$0822 so the next entry skips all this. Falls into joust_restart.

Per-joust set-up (every entry, including PRACTICE AGAIN): reset the stack, blank the screen, clear zero page $12-$C5 (clear_zero_page $14AE, which also clears the opponent choice $35), build the quarter-square multiply tables ($14BA) and the two sprite-mirroring tables ($14EA), install the raster interrupt ($0A63), reset the sound driver ($22C8), put both skaters in state 0 at their start positions (start_skater $1A68 with $29 = 0 and $40). If the event manager has made the second skater the computer (slot_b_is_cpu $FE0F = $FF, written at $FA46 and $FF7B, as in practice) the opponent-choice screen runs first (show_choice_screen $0AD9, choose_opponent $2086, blank_screen). Then setup_joust ($099A), show the pool picture ($0AA0), enable interrupts and fall into the main loop.

Main loop; everything else runs in the raster interrupt. If music_off_request ($42) is set by the Commodore-key toggle, reset the sound driver (silencing all three voices) and clear it. If the game's sound ring has entries (read index $C4 differs from write index $C3), take the next ID (sound_ring_pop $215A) and pass it to queue_sound_id ($2306). If the interrupt has counted a frame in $C5, run one tick of the sound driver (update_sid_voices $233D) and count it off. Loops for ever; the event ends by JMP $FE06 from inside the interrupt.

Load and unpack both pictures. File $16 (the opponent-choice screen, run-length packed) loads at $4000; unpack_rle ($2169) expands it to $8000 until the end address the loader returned ($16/$17). With the I/O banked out ($01 = $24, interrupts off) it copies $1F40 bytes to the bitmap at $C000-$DF3F (RAM under the I/O area, read by the VIC in bank 3), $3E8 colour-RAM bytes to $E000 and $3E8 screen bytes to $E400. Then file $17 (the pool, also packed) loads at $4000, unpacks to $8000 and is copied to the bitmap at $4000-$5F3F, the colour source at $6000 and the screen matrix at $6400 (bank 1); the last copy is a tail call of copy_block. The packed files and the $8000 scratch copy are both overwritten afterwards (files $18 and $19 load at $8000).
Operand of LDY #$03 at $0953 (the $3E8-byte screen copy). The resident RESET vector in RAM, $FFFC/$FFFD, happens to hold $0954, which is why a symbol appears here; nothing in the joust jumps to it.

Load the skater graphics: file $18 (124 frame descriptors of 24 bytes) at $8000, keeping its end address ($8BA0) in sprite_shape_base $2FD8/$2FD9; file $19 (the packed sprite rows that the descriptors point into) straight after it at $8BA0; file $1A (22 ready-made sprites) at $7000-$757F, sprite blocks $C0-$D5 of bank 1. Then sprite multicolour 1 = $0A (light red) and multicolour 2 = 0 (black).

Point $1F/$20 at frame descriptor A: $8000 + A * $18 (multiply_8x8 $1514 with Y = $18). Each 24-byte descriptor in file $18 describes the four sprites of one skater pose; see build_skater_sprites $16CF and place_skater_sprites $0C82.
Add A to the pointer $12/$13. Nothing in this load calls it (no JSR, JMP or address of $0990 found in code or tables); the same routine is in High Jump at $096D, also uncalled.

Set up one joust: if the music is on ($FE10 = 0) queue sound 1, the music, through the game's ring. Copy the first skater's name pointer ($FE00/$FE01) to $43/$44 and the second slot's ($FE09/$FE0A) to $83/$84. Status line (text row 0, hires): colours from status_colours_a ($2EC9) into screen row 0, then the inline text at $09C4 (15 spaces and '-- PRESS YOUR BUTTON -- ') from column 0, then the first skater's name over its start. $FE02 becomes the colour of the first skater's last body sprite ($2EB6). setup_opponent ($1CE0) sets the second skater's name, colours and computer play. Then the intro counter $30 = 3, all sprites off ($31 = 0), sprite buffer blocks $B0 and $B4 ($4B, $8B), both skaters' pose = $2A7D's first entry, build both skaters' sprites, copy the five pass-counter sprites ($2D33-$2E72) to $6A00-$6B3F (blocks $A8-$AC), first skater on joystick port 2 ($45 = 0, CIA 1 port A), second on port 1 ($85 = 1, port B), and joystick histories $56/$96 = 0, $57/$97 = $FF.

Inline argument of print_inline ($1411) at $09C1: 40 characters, '               -- PRESS YOUR BUTTON -- ', zero-terminated; printed into the bitmap's text row 0. The first skater's name is printed over the leading spaces straight after ($09FA).

setup_joust continued after its inline text: print the first skater's name at column 0 (set_print_column $1461, print_string $1427 through $43/$44); copy the slot's attribute $FE02 into the first skater's last body colour ($2EB6); setup_opponent; intro step $30 = 3, sprites off; sprite buffers $B0/$B4; both poses from drop_in_poses' first byte; build both skaters' sprites (build_skater_sprites $16CF); copy the five pass-counter sprites, 63 bytes each, from $2D33/$2D73/$2DB3/$2DF3/$2E33 to $6A00/$6A40/$6A80/$6AC0/$6B00; joystick ports and histories.

Operand byte of LDA $2DB3,X (the third pass-digit sprite). The NMI vector in RAM, $FFFA/$FFFB, holds $0A3A, so the disassembler puts a symbol in the middle of this instruction; nothing in the joust jumps here.

Install the raster interrupt: interrupts off, $01 = $25, CIA 1 interrupts masked ($DC0D = $7F) and acknowledged, wait for the raster to wrap (wait_frame_wrap $0A95), band 0 ($1E = 0) with the compare line from raster_lines ($2A16, $FB), the vector $FFFE/$FFFF = raster_irq ($0B84), raster interrupt enabled ($D01A = 1).
Wait until the raster line's low byte ($D012) goes down between two reads, which happens once a frame when the counter returns to line 0 (and at line 256). Same code as High Jump's $0A45.

Show the pool: border and background black, copy the 1000 colour bytes at $6000 to colour RAM $D800 (copy_block), $D018 = $90 (screen $6400, bitmap $4000 in bank 1), $DD00 bank 1 (bits 0-1 = 2), $D016 = $18 (multicolour, 40 columns), $D011 = $3B (bitmap mode, display on, 25 rows).

Show the opponent-choice screen: border and background black, the 1000 colour bytes at $E000 to colour RAM, $D018 = $90 with bank 3 ($DD00 bits 0-1 = 0): screen $E400, bitmap $C000. Multicolour bitmap on. Copies the arrow sprite (choice_arrow_sprite $2E73) to $E800, sprite block $A0 of bank 3.
Copy Y*256+X bytes from the read pointer $12/$13 to the write pointer $14/$15 (X = 0 counts as 256 in the low part); counters $18/$19. Same code as High Jump's $0A8A.

Unreferenced: copy_block with each byte taken from JSR $FFCF (the KERNAL's CHRIN address) instead of memory; with the ROMs banked out that address is RAM inside archive_event. No caller in this load; the same dead routine is in High Jump at $0AA2.
Unreferenced: write Y*256+X zero bytes through the write pointer $14/$15. No caller in this load (High Jump's copy at $0ABA is also uncalled).
Return the byte at ($12) in A and advance the pointer $12/$13; leaves Y = 0. Used by copy_block, print_inline, lookup_path_xy and unpack_rle.
Store A at ($14) and advance the pointer $14/$15; leaves Y = 0. Byte sink of copy_block and unpack_rle.

Unreferenced: CLI, JSR $FFE7 and loop on JSR $FFE4 until non-zero, a KERNAL key wait (CLALL, GETIN) left from development. No caller; with the ROMs out those addresses are inside archive_event's instructions.

Raster interrupt entry (vector $FFFE): save A, X, Y, acknowledge the VIC ($D019), take the handler of the current band $1E from raster_handlers ($2A12), patch it into the JSR at $0B9F and call it, then restore and RTI. Two bands: 0 at line $FB (band0_status_irq $0BB6), 1 at line $38 (band1_play_irq $0D8B). Each handler sets the next band's line itself (next_raster_band $0BA8).
JSR operand rewritten at $0B96/$0B9C with the band's handler from raster_handlers; $0BB6 as saved, the band-0 handler.
Low byte of the JSR operand at $0B9F, written at $0B96 from raster_handlers ($2A12,X); $0BA1, the high byte, at $0B9C from $2A13,X.
High byte of the band handler JSR operand, written at $0B9C.
Advance $1E to the next band (raster_next_band $2A18: 0 -> 1 -> 0) and set the raster compare $D012 to its line (raster_lines $2A16: $FB, $38).

Band 0, raster line $FB (bottom border): multicolour off ($D016 bit 4 clear) so the top text row, row 0, is drawn hires; next band; set up all sprites for the coming frame (setup_sprites $0BDA); count the frame in $23/$24 ($178B); poll RUN/STOP (poll_run_stop $2104, which can end the event) and the Commodore key (poll_music_key $2120); run the pole-swing timers ($2073); step the random generator ($176F); count a sound tick in $C5 for the main loop; and latch the pole holder for this frame ($2B = $2C).

Sprite registers for one frame: enable mask from $31 ($00 before the joust, $70/$0F/$FF during the introduction), all sprites in front of the picture ($D01B = 0) and multicolour ($D01C = $FF). The pole colour of both skaters ($2EB3, $2EB7) cycles through pole_flash_colours ($2FC4) by the swing timer $33. The skater in front ($2A, chosen by depth in set_draw_order $1A70) gets the low sprite numbers, so it is drawn over the other: colours (skater_sprite_colours $0C47), pointers (skater_sprite_pointers $0C65), positions (place_skater_sprites $0C82) for it, then the other. The last sprite used shows the pass counter, block $A8 + $2E (the boxed digits 1-5 at $6A00), placed by place_pass_counter ($0D65). Then the collected X high bits, X-expand and Y-expand masks ($1B, $1C, $1D) go to $D010, $D01D and $D017.
Pointer for the pass counter sprite: $A8 + passes_left ($2E, 4 down to 0), so it shows the boxed digit 5 down to 1; Y has counted the skaters' sprites, so it takes the next free sprite.

Write one skater's sprite colours from sprite_colours ($2EB3) into $D027,Y onward: skater X = 0 uses entries 0-3, X = $40 entries 4-7. The skater holding the pole ($2B) gets all four (entry 0 or 4 is the pole colour, which flashes); the other skips it and gets three. Advances Y.
Write one skater's sprite pointers ($4C-$4E,X, and $4F,X for the pole holder) into the screen's pointer bytes $67F8,Y onward, advancing Y. The pointers were collected by build_skater_sprites ($16CF).

Position one skater's sprites. If $52,X is negative (knocked off, state $0A) the body uses the flying pose $7B,X at $76/$77 (X low, high), $78 (Y) with facing $75,X; otherwise the riding pose $6B,X at $66/$67/$68 with facing $65,X. Each sprite is placed from its 6-byte part of the frame descriptor (place_sprite_part $0D10): the pole holder places parts 0-2, the other skips part 0 (the pole) and places parts 1-2; the last part (3, the skateboard) always comes from the riding pose and position, so the board rolls on when the rider is thrown off. $18 counts sprites, $19 counts sprite register pairs.

Place sprite $19/2 from the descriptor part at ($1F): Y = base Y ($28) + part byte 4. Facing left ($1A bit 7 set): X = base X ($26/$27) + byte 3. Facing right: X = base - byte 3, minus 24 more when the part is X-expanded (byte 5 bit 5), which mirrors the sprite's position about the skater. The ninth X bit is rotated into $1B, and byte 5 bits 5 and 4 into the X-expand ($1C) and Y-expand ($1D) masks.

Place the pass counter sprite by the pole holder: entry 0 (holder = first skater) or 1 from pass_counter_pos ($2EC3 X low, $2EC5 X high bit, $2EC7 Y): X $138 when the first skater holds the pole, $20 when the second does, Y $52 either way. Colour 1 (white); the X high bit goes into $1B, and the expand masks get a zero bit.

Band 1, raster line $38: wait for line $3A and a short delay, switch multicolour on ($D016 bit 4) for the pool picture below the status row, set the next band, then run the game: update both skaters (update_skater $0DEE with $29 = 0, then $40), work out which is in front (set_draw_order $1A70), test for a hit (check_hit $1A85). When the skaters are within reach (check_hit returns carry set): if a computer opponent plays ($35 non-zero) its newly-pressed byte $97 is cleared (every bit 'just pressed') and pole_swing_start ($205A) runs for it, so a computer holding the pole swings the moment it is in reach, timers permitting; then, if the pole holder is mid-swing ($33 non-zero) the holder ($2B) scores ($60,X + 1), the other skater is knocked off (state $0A), the scores are reprinted (print_scores $1B27) and sound $0C is queued. Finally $5F/$9F keep each skater's animation step $59/$99 for the next frame.

Update skater $29 for one frame: read its controls and run its state handler (read_controls_and_run_state $0E28). Then rebuild its sprites (build_skater_sprites $16CF) if its pose or facing changed, or (knocked off) its flying pose changed, comparing with last frame's $48/$49/$4A,X; a facing change also sets $5E,X and $39 to $FF. Store this frame's pose, facing and flying pose for the next comparison.

Read skater X's controls and run its state. The second skater ($29 = $40) is played by the computer when an opponent was chosen ($35 non-zero) and the introduction is over ($30 = 0): its joystick byte comes from cpu_joystick ($1D4F). Otherwise the joystick port $45,X (0 = $DC00, port 2; 1 = $DC01, port 1) is read. $56,X keeps the raw byte and $57,X the newly-pressed bits (a bit is 0 when that direction or fire is down now and was up last frame; active low like the port). Then the handler for state $55,X is taken from state_handlers ($2AE9), patched into the JSR at $0E5B and called; afterwards pole_swing_start ($205A) lets the holder start a swing.
JSR operand rewritten at $0E52/$0E58 with the current state's handler from state_handlers ($2AE9); assembled as $FFFF.
Low byte of the state handler JSR operand at $0E5B, written at $0E52 from state_handlers ($2AE9,Y); the high byte $0E5D at $0E58 from $2AEA,Y.
High byte of the state handler JSR operand, written at $0E58.

State 0, standing on the deck at the start of a round (start positions $56 and $1CC, the top of the left and right walls). Looks up the path point ($146D). During the introduction ($30 non-zero) runs intro_step ($1BFA) instead. Otherwise, with no drop-in under way ($58/$59 = 0): the skater without the pole may step along the deck with up/down while the other is also on the deck (deck_depth_move $1977). Fire (newly pressed) starts the drop-in only when this skater's pole status is settled ($2B = $2C) and the other skater is neither knocked off (state $0A) nor climbing out (state $14); the pole holder must also wait until the other has left the deck (states 0 and $10). The drop-in is 8 steps of 6 frames ($58, $59), poses drop_in_poses ($2A7D, holder $2A85), then state 2 (start_riding $12C9) with $5E = 1, $51 = 0. With no fire, a 1-in-$55 chance each frame (random_below $1782) starts a fidget: $5A = 0 or 1 at random, state $10. Every frame sets the screen position (skater_screen_pos $131B) and the pose.

State $10, a fidget on the deck: the pole holder, or fire, ends it at once (back to state 0 and its handler). Otherwise allows deck_depth_move, looks up the path point and screen position, and steps an animation of 8 frames per step through fidget_poses_a ($2ACA, 19 steps, $5A = 0) or fidget_poses_b ($2ADD, 10 steps, $5A = 1), the lengths in fidget_lengths ($2AE7); at the end, state 0.
End the fidget: state 0, animation counters cleared, and run the state-0 handler this frame.

State 2, riding the pool: up/down moves the skater across the pool (depth_controls $1962, up = towards the far side), move along the path under gravity and set the screen position (move_skater $12E8), friction (speed_friction $192A). Low on the wall (path Y $50 >= $96): the pose comes from the 3-byte rows of riding_pose_rows ($2A35, mirrored set $2A44), chosen by height (thresholds $BA, $D6, $E3, $EC, $FF) and by whether the skater rides backwards ($51) and climbs or descends; the pole holder's poses are $42 further on. In the band nearest the coping (Y $96-$B9) the pose depends on the trick queued in $5E (lean_poses $2A1A/$2A1E, holder $2A22/$2A26) and $5E is settled by choose_trick ($19D2); below that, left/right presses are read into $5C/$5D (read_trick_input $199F). Above the coping (Y < $96, branch $0FD1): see $0FD1.

At the top of a wall. For the skater without the pole: one pass is used up ($2E - 1, sound $14); when the fifth is gone ($2E below 0) this skater takes the pole ($2C = X), the pass counter is reset to 4 (reset_round_timers $1B0E) and sound $10 plays. Then every skater goes to the state the queued trick asks for: wall_trick_states ($2A2A) indexed by $5E (0 air turn = state 4, 1 = state 6, 2 = state $0E, 3 = state $12). $2F is set non-zero by $17ED and $1B1A and never cleared, so its test at $0FD5 always passes.

State $0A, knocked off by the pole. $52 = $FF, so the body is drawn from the flying pose $7B at $76-$78 while the board (sprite part 3) goes on along the path: drift across the pool by $6F (depth_drift $1A21), move the board along the path, double friction, board pose by height from riding_pose_rows' second column (or lean_poses' first entry). While $5A = 0 the body flies (body_fly $16A8: velocity $79/$7A, gravity $10 a frame) through the four pose frames knock_fly_poses ($2A96), one step every $61 frames (4-8, random), until its Y reaches $F0; then it lands: $79 = $FF, sounds $0F and $16. From then on ($1066) it slides to a stop (body_slide $10C3) through one of three 7-frame tumbles chosen in $62 (knock_tumble_ptrs $2AAF), 10 frames a step. After the tumble, once the other skater is back on the deck or climbing out (states 0, $10, $14), fire returns this skater to the deck (state 0).
Slide the thrown body: add the decaying speed $79,X to the X fraction $80,X and carry into $73,X (held at 255), then lower $79 by 5 to a minimum of 0.

State 4, in the air above the coping (trick 0): left/right spin the skater through its 16 facing poses (spin_controls $18C2), up/down tilt its path across the pool (tilt_controls $1901), move along the path. On coming back below the coping (Y >= $96) the skater rides backwards ($51 = $FF) if it landed facing between poses 4 and $0B (mod $41: the holder's poses are offset), forwards otherwise, and returns to state 2. Poses are never judged as a fall: any landing is accepted.

State 6, a trick held at the coping (trick 1; move_skater clamps Y at $96): up/down still tilt; steps through lip_trick_poses ($2A53, backwards rider $2A58, holder +$42) one step every 3 frames. On the last step: without fire the skater drops back in (state 8); with fire held and left or right newly pressed, a turn (state $0C) whose direction $5A is the facing (right) or its complement (left). Falling below the coping also gives state 8.
State 8, coming back from the lip trick: lip_trick_poses in reverse, one step every 3 frames; after the fifth, start_riding ($12C9: state 2 from the coping position of this side).

State $0C, a turn at the coping: 8 steps of 3 frames through lip_turn_poses ($2A5D/$2A65/$2A6D/$2A75, chosen by riding backwards $51 and turn direction $5A; the holder's poses are $41 or $42 further on). At the end the trick is cleared ($5E = 0), the riding direction flips ($51) and start_riding puts the skater back at the coping.

State $0E (trick 2): moves the skater across the pool each frame (add $7F, or $81 when riding backwards, to the depth fraction, adjust_depth $19FD), move along the path, 9 steps of 2 frames through slide_turn_poses ($2A8D, read backwards when riding backwards; holder +$41). At the end the riding direction flips and start_riding.

State $12, climbing out of the pool after knocking the other skater off (trick 3, chosen by choose_trick when the other is in state $0A): 4 steps of 6 frames through climb_poses ($2AB5, backwards $2AB9), then sound $0D and state $14.

State $14, on the deck after climbing out: steps through wait_poses ($2ABD) every 4 frames for 12 steps and keeps the computer's reaction delay at $1E ($36); after that, fire returns the skater to state 0. Resets the swing cooldown $34 every frame, so no swing can start.
Set state 2 (set_state $1792) and fall into reset_to_coping.

Put skater $29 at the coping of its own side: position $71/$72 = $56 on the left (facing $65 positive) or $1CC on the right. Profile entry $56 is X 42, Y 150, where the vertical wall meets the transition.

Move skater $29 along the path and work out its screen position: X = 0 here (the alternative entry $12ED, LDX #$10, would do the same for the thrown body at offset $10 but nothing jumps there). path_physics ($165D) adds gravity and moves the position, lookup_path_xy ($146D) reads the profile; $50,X keeps the path Y. While the skater is not knocked off and its queued trick needs it (trick_holds_lip $2A2E[$5E] non-zero) Y is held at $96, so lip tricks stay at the coping instead of flying. Then skater_screen_pos.
LDX #$10: alternative entry of move_skater for the thrown body's fields ($10 bytes on); no jump, branch or table reaches $12ED.

Screen position of skater $29 (entry $1320: of its thrown body, fields $10 further on). With the depth scale $6D/$6E (8.8 fixed point, $C0-$108) as multiplier (multiply_8x8 $1514): X = $B7 + (path X - $B7) * scale, pulling the skater towards the pool's centre line as it goes further away; Y = 7 + (path Y - 7) * scale - 10. Then the left half is offset by -11 and the right half mirrored as $163 - X, giving the 9-bit screen X in $66/$67 and the Y in $68.
Entry of skater_screen_pos for the thrown body: X = $29 + $10, so it reads $73/$74 and $7D/$7E and writes $76-$78.

One frame of spin, used for left: on the left half (facing positive) add $47 to the spin fraction $53, on carry step the pose down (0-$0F, wrapping), and move $33 across the pool (adjust_depth $19FD); on the right half take spin_step_right's subtracting path ($13C8). So the same direction spins the other way on the other side, and every spin also drifts the skater across the pool.

One frame of spin, used for right: on the left half subtract $47 from $53, on borrow step the pose up (wrapping at $10) and adjust_depth by $CD (-$33); on the right half take the adding path at $13A7.

Unreferenced debugging printer: print the high nibble of A as a hex digit at text column Y (entry $13E7 prints the low nibble), suppressing leading zeros through $25 (a zero with $25 clear prints a space), the glyph from hex_digits ($2D23). No JSR, JMP or address of $13E3-$1407 exists in this load; $25 is not used elsewhere.
Low-nibble entry of the unreferenced hex printer: AND #$0F, then as print_hex_digit_hi.
Load file $15, the 64-glyph font, to $6800-$69FF (tail call of load_file $F230).

Print the zero-terminated text that follows the JSR at text column A of row 0: set the glyph pointer (glyph_column $1461), pull the return address into $12/$13, step past the JSR's last byte, print (print_string $1427) and push the address of the terminator, so RTS resumes after it. Call sites: $09C1, $1B9C (dead code), $1C2A, $1CBB; their arguments are typed as text.
Draw the zero-terminated string at ($12) into the bitmap from the glyph pointer $14/$15, one 8-byte character cell per character; each byte keeps its low six bits (screen-code order of the font).
Copy glyph A (0-63) from the font at $6800 + A*8 to the bitmap cell at ($14) and advance $14/$15 by 8 (one character cell).
Set the glyph pointer $14/$15 to $4000 + A*8: character cell A of text row 0 in the pool bitmap. Only row 0 is ever printed to.

Path point of skater X: from the position $71/$72 (0-$222) take entry s (left half, s < $111) or $222 - s (right half, mirrored) of the path profile ($2AFF, two bytes an entry) into $63,X (path X) and $64,X (path Y), leaving $12/$13 pointing past it. The half is rotated into bit 7 of $65,X (set on the right half), which is the skater's facing everywhere else. The profile is the same 273-entry table as High Jump's ramp.
Zero $12-$C5: all of the joust's zero-page state, both skater records and the opponent choice $35.
Build the quarter-square tables for multiply_8x8: floor(n*n/4) for n = 0-511, low bytes at $0400-$05FF and high bytes at $0600-$07FF, by adding n/2 each step. Same code as High Jump's $1310.

Build the two mirroring tables: reverse_bits ($2FEA-$30E9), each byte with its eight bits reversed (for hires sprites, used only by the dead copy at $1537), and reverse_pairs ($30EA-$31E9), each byte with its four bit pairs reversed (multicolour pixels), used by sprite_part_mirrored ($1580).

A * Y to a 16-bit product, A = low, Y = high, with the quarter-square tables: the two LDAs patch their low bytes with A ($1528, $152F) so they read square[A + Y]; X = |Y - A|; product = square[A + Y] - square[|Y - A|]. Uses X.
Low byte of LDA $0403,Y's operand, rewritten with A at $1514: the read becomes square_lo[A + Y] (the +3 assembled into the operand is replaced).
Low byte of LDA $0603,Y's operand, rewritten with A at $1517: square_hi[A + Y].

Unreferenced earlier copy of sprite_part_mirrored ($1580) that mirrors with reverse_bits ($2FEA, single-pixel order) instead of reverse_pairs: byte for byte the same routine otherwise. Nothing calls it, which is why reverse_bits is built but never read.

Build one sprite from the current descriptor part ($1F) mirrored left-right, for a skater facing left (on the left half of the pool): get_part_source ($15F6). A part marked as a ready-made sprite gets pointer value + $CB (the mirrored skateboard sprites of file $1A, blocks $CB-$D5) and uses no buffer. Otherwise bytes above the part's last byte ($18) up to 62 are cleared and each 3-byte row is copied with its bytes swapped end for end and each byte's pixel pairs reversed (reverse_pairs $30EA); then next_part_block ($1617).

Build one sprite from the current descriptor part as stored, for a skater facing right: a ready-made sprite gets pointer value + $C0 (blocks $C0-$CA); otherwise clear bytes above the part's length and copy bytes 0-$18 from the shape data, then next_part_block.

Read the current descriptor part ($1F): bytes 0-1 are an offset into the shape data of file $19, added to sprite_shape_base ($2FD8/$2FD9, $8BA0) into $12/$13, byte 2 the index of the shape's last byte into $18; carry clear. If byte 1 has bit 7 set the part is a ready-made sprite instead: A = byte 0 (0-10), carry set.

After building a sprite: step $1F to the next descriptor part (+6), the buffer pointer $14/$15 to the next 64-byte block, record block number $1C in the skater's pointer list ($4C + $1D) and advance both.
Move skater $29 one step further away: depth scale $6D/$6E - 1, not below $00C0 (the far side of the pool).
Move skater $29 one step nearer: depth scale + 1 while below $0108 (the near side).

Gravity and motion along the path for the record at X: if the profile pointer is below $2D03 (entry 258, so the read 16 entries ahead stays in the table), the slope is the path Y 16 entries ahead minus here, added to the speed $69/$6A (subtracted on the right half), so the skater accelerates down the walls and slows climbing. Then position $70 (fraction)/$71/$72 += speed (sign-extended). The same scheme as High Jump's ramp physics.
One frame of the thrown body's flight: X $73,X + 1 (held at 255), Y $74 (fraction $80) += vertical speed $79/$7A, which then gains $10 (gravity).

Rebuild skater $29's sprite shapes into its other buffer: flip $4B,X between two sets of blocks ($B0/$B8 for the first skater, $B4/$BC for the second: $6C00-$6FFF of bank 1), so the shown set is never half drawn; $14/$15 = $4000 + block * 64, the pointer list $4C,X restarts. Riding: the pose $6B gives the descriptor; the pole holder builds all four parts, the other skips part 0 (the pole). Knocked off: parts 1-2 (holder 1-3) of the flying pose $7B with facing $75, then part 3, the board, of the riding pose with facing $65. Facing left (bit 7 clear) uses sprite_part_mirrored, facing right sprite_part_plain.

Knocked off: the flying pose's parts. The skip of part 0 here is unconditional, so for a pole holder it would build parts 1-3 while place_skater_sprites places parts 0-2; only the skater without the pole is ever knocked off (state $0A is set only at $0DD6, for the other skater), so the mismatch never shows.
Pseudo-random byte: shift-and-subtract step on $21/$22, plus $22, XORed with the frame counter $23. Called once a frame by the interrupt and by random_below.
Random number 0 to A-1: random_byte * A, keeping the high byte (multiply_8x8).
Frame counter $23/$24 + 1 (16 bits). $23 times the prompt flashing, the menu arrow colours and the computer's alternate-frame fire.

Enter state A for skater $29 ($55,X) and reset its animation ($58, $59). State 0 (back on the deck): $5A = 1-20 at random (the computer's drop-in delay), computer pause $36 = 20 frames, facing left for the first skater and right for the second, position at its coping, depth scale $00C8. If the other skater is also on the deck (state 0 or $10) the round is over: if the match is decided ($32) the event ends (end_event $2145); otherwise the pole goes to the skater who did not start the last round with it ($2D XOR $40 into $2C) and the round timers reset. State 2: speed $0280 rightwards on the left half or $FD80 leftwards on the right, trick and spin cleared. State $0A (knocked off): the body is launched from the rider's place with vertical speed $FEE0 (upwards), facing and depth copied, sideways drift $6F = $7A, or $86 when near the near side (far_side_test), animation interval $61 = 4-8 and tumble $62 = 0-2 at random, sound $0E.
Left held during an air turn: $5A = $C0 (spin left) unless a right spin ($E0) is running, which it stops ($5A AND $A0).
Right held: $5A = $E0 (spin right) unless a left spin ($C0) is running, which it stops.
Up held in the air: $5B = $C0 (drift away) unless a downward drift ($E0) is running, which it stops.
Down held: $5B = $E0 (drift nearer) unless an upward drift is running, which it stops.
Clear bit 6 of $5B: the drift stops but the direction bits stay.
Clear bit 6 of $5A: the spin stops.

Air turn controls: take the pole holder's pose offset ($41) off, latch left/right into $5A, then spin one step a frame while bit 6 of $5A is set (spin_step_left for %10, spin_step_right for %11), and put the offset back.
In the air, up/down latch a drift across the pool in $5B; while it runs, adjust_depth by $81 (away) or $7F (nearer) each frame.
Friction: move the speed $69/$6A one unit (1/256) towards zero. The alternative entry $192F (LDX #$10) would apply it to the thrown body's $79/$7A; only the dead code at $1953 uses it.
LDX #$10: entry of speed_friction for the fields $10 on (the thrown body's speed $79/$7A), reached only from the dead code at $1953-$1961.

Unreferenced: nested JSRs that fall through into one another ($1953 JSR $1959 twice, $1959 JSR $195C, $195C JSR $195F, $195F JMP $192F) and so apply speed_friction to the thrown body's speed twelve times. Nothing calls it.
Inside the dead body_friction_x12: JSR $195C, entered by the JSRs at $1953 and $1956 and by falling through.
Inside body_friction_x12: JSR $195F, then falls into it.
Inside body_friction_x12: JMP $192F, speed_friction for the thrown body.
Up held: depth_farther; down held: depth_nearer (raw joystick bits in $56,X).
On the deck, the skater without the pole may move along the edge with up/down while the other skater is also on the deck (state 0 or $10).

Low on the wall, a newly pressed left or right queues the trick for the next wall top: pressing against the direction of travel (left while the speed is positive, right while negative) sets $5C, with the direction of travel sets $5D (the other is cleared).
Against the direction of travel: $5C = $FF, $5D = 0 (trick 2, state $0E).
With the direction of travel: $5C = 0, $5D = $FF (trick 1, state 6).
Set the queued trick $5E for the next wall top: 3 (climb out, state $12) if the other skater is knocked off; else 2 if $5C, 1 if $5D, 0 (air turn) otherwise (trick_codes $2A32-$2A34).
Add the signed fraction A to the depth fraction $6C,X and carry into the depth scale (depth_nearer on a carry from a positive A, depth_farther on a borrow from a negative one).
$1F/$20 += A: step through a frame descriptor (6 bytes a part).
The knocked-off skater's sideways drift: add $6F,X to the depth fraction (with carries into the scale) and decay $6F by 2 towards zero.
Carry set if skater $29's depth scale is $E4 or more (near the near edge).
Starting speed for state 2: A/Y = $80/$02 ($0280) on the left half, $80/$FD ($FD80) on the right.
Reset the round timers and put skater $29 in state 0.
$2A = the skater drawn in front: 0 if the first skater's depth ($6C-$6E, 24 bits) is at least the second's (nearer the viewer), else $40.

Carry set when the skaters can touch: not both on the deck (states 0/$10), neither climbing out or waiting ($12, $14) nor knocked off ($0A); depth scales within 8 of each other (-8 < difference < 8); screen X ($66/$67) less than 256 apart; and |screen Y difference| + |screen X difference| below 15 pixels.
New round or new holder: passes left $2E = 4, swing timer $33 = 0, cooldown $34 = $20, $2F = $20, and $FF in both skaters' last pose and flying pose ($48/$88, $4A/$8A) so their sprites are rebuilt.
Print both score fields in row 0: the first skater's at column 0, the second's at column $25 (score_text $1B3C).

Score field for skater X: while both scores ($60, $A0) are below 3, the score as '-n-'. From 3 on, by the lead over the other: behind '---', level 'TIE', one ahead 'ADV', two or more 'WIN', which ends the match ($32 = $FF) and stores 1 as the result: $FE03 for the first skater, $FE0C for the second. So the match is first to three points with a lead of two, like deuce in tennis. Strings: score_strings ($2F89) + 4 * index.

Unreferenced: set the status colours from $2F19, print the '- -  VS  - -' row (inline text at $1B9F), then both names at columns 3 and $16 and the scores: the same as intro steps 2 and 1 ($1C1F, $1C5C) done at once. Nothing calls it.
Inline text of the unreferenced $1B93: '- -', spaces, 'VS', spaces, '- -' (40 characters), zero-terminated.

Rest of the unreferenced print_vs_row ($1B93) after its inline text: first name at column 3, second at column $16, then JMP print_scores. intro_show_names ($1C5C) does the same work in the routine that runs; this copy is never reached.
Copy 40 colour bytes from (X/Y) to screen row 0 ($6400-$6427): ink and paper of the hires status line.

One frame of the introduction, run from the second skater's state-0 handler while $30 is non-zero (returns at once for the first skater): keeps the swing cooldown and computer pause set. $30 = 3 (intro_wait_buttons $1C98): only sprites 0-3 shown ($31 = $0F); waits for fire. $30 = 2 (two humans only): sprites $70, waits for the second skater's fire with the prompt flashing, then (with $30 = 2 or after step 3 against the computer) step to 1: status colours $2F19 and the '- -  VS  - -' row (inline text $1C2D). $30 = 1 ($1C5C): both names (columns 3 and $16) and the scores, all sprites on ($31 = $FF), and $30 = 0: play starts.
Inline argument of print_inline at $1C2A: '- -', 17 spaces, 'VS', 15 spaces, '- -' (40 characters), zero-terminated: the status row between the prompt and the names.
Border black (the $D020 write at the end of the VS step).
Intro step 1: $30 = 0, print the first skater's name at column 3 and the second's at column $16 (print_string through $43/$44 and $83/$84), print the scores and show all sprites.
Status line colours alternate every 16 frames (bit 4 of the frame counter $23) between status_colours_a ($2EC9) and status_colours_b ($2EF1): the flashing PRESS YOUR BUTTON.

Intro step 3: sprites 0-3 on. The first skater's fire (newly pressed) moves on; otherwise the second skater's fire moves on after swapping the two joystick ports ($45/$85), so whoever presses first plays the left-hand skater; neither: flash the prompt. Against the computer step 2 is skipped ($1C1F). With two humans the prompt stays and the second skater's name is printed over the first's (16 spaces, inline at $1CBE, then the name at column 0), asking the other player to press.
Inline argument of print_inline at $1CBB: 16 spaces, zero-terminated, clearing the first name before the second skater's is printed.
After the 16 blanks: set column 0 and print the second skater's name ($83/$84) where the first one was, so the status line asks the second player to press.

Set up the second skater from the opponent choice $35: 0 (two humans) takes the name from the event manager's second slot ($FE09/$FE0A); 1-3 the names POSEUR PETE, AGGRO' EDDIE, LESTER (opponent_names $2F61). Colours of its three body sprites from opponent_colour_1/2/3 ($2F6D, $2F71, $2F75; $FF in the last means the second slot's colour byte $FE0B). The computer's decision interval $38 from opponent_interval ($2F69: 15, 7, 1 frames) and its depth distances: $3A/$3B = +/- opponent_chase_range ($2F7D), $3C/$3D = +/- opponent_evade_far ($2F81), $3E/$3F = +/- opponent_evade_near ($2F85).
Interrupts off, display off ($D011 bit 4 clear), wait for the raster to wrap, border black. Leaves interrupts disabled.

The computer's joystick byte (active low, as from the port) for skater $29. While the pause $36 runs (set on returning to the deck, during the knock-off and the climb-out) it presses nothing and counts down. Otherwise it decides only every $37 frames, reloaded from the opponent's interval $38 (15 for Pete, 7 for Eddie, 1 for Lester), repeating its last byte ($56,X) in between. A decision starts from nothing pressed in $18: the pole holder steers across the pool towards the player (cpu_chase $1D87), the other steers away (cpu_evade $1DB6), then the opponent's own routine adds fire and left/right (cpu_personality $1E01).

Computer with the pole: depth difference d = own scale - player's. d >= +range ($3A): press up (further away); d < -range: press down; otherwise neither. Ranges: Pete 12, Eddie 5, Lester 3 scale units, so Lester lines up most closely.

Computer without the pole: keep a depth distance from the player between the near limit ($3E: 8, 10, 15) and the far limit ($3C: 20, 30, 45 for Pete, Eddie, Lester): beyond the far limit do nothing, between them move away (up when the player is nearer, down when further), inside the near limit run for the open side (cpu_evade_side $1DED).
Too close: press up if the player is near the near edge (scale >= $E4), otherwise down.
Dispatch on the opponent $35: 1 Poseur Pete ($1E14), 2 Aggro Eddie ($1FAB), anything else Lester ($1E97).

Poseur Pete's controls by his own state: on the deck, knocked off or waiting (0, $10, $0A, $14) fire on even frames (drop in at once, get up at once); in the air (4) spin left or right according to the depth direction already chosen and his side; riding (2), once after each change of half ($39), and at a lip trick (6) every decision: left, nothing or right at random (cpu_random_turn $1E87), which queues a random trick. States 8, $0C, $0E, $12: nothing.
In the air: with up chosen spin one way and with down the other, mirrored by the side of the pool (clearing bit 2, left, or bit 3, right, of $18); neither: no spin.
Press left, nothing or right at random: $18 AND cpu_turn_masks ($2FC1: $FB, $FF, $F7) [random_below 3].

Lester's controls (also any opponent number above 2). It first calls $1F73, an RTS: the distance-based range setter behind it ($1F74) is switched off. On the deck with the pole he waits until the player has crossed to the right half; then drops in at once if the player is moving left, otherwise when the player is above path Y $8E and his own random delay $5A has run out. Without the pole, knocked off or waiting: fire on even frames. Air: as Pete. Riding, once per change of half while passes remain: random if the player is on the deck, else left or right towards (with the pole) or away from (without) the player's side. Lip trick: fire depending on the player's direction and height ($1F54).

Lester at the lip (state 6): with the pole, hold fire (alternate frames) unless the player's speed sign differs from his own facing; without it, hold fire when they differ or when the player is above path Y $95.
RTS: Lester's first call. The routine after it never runs.

Dead code behind the RTS at $1F73: would set Lester's near evade limit $3E/$3F from the distance along the path between the skaters, |pos1 - pos2| / 16 - $23 (at least 1) + 5. Disabled; $3E/$3F keep setup_opponent's value.

Aggro Eddie: as Lester but simpler. On the deck with the pole he drops in as soon as the player is on the right half and above path Y $8E (no random delay, no direction test); without the pole, knocked off or waiting: fire on even frames; air: as Pete; riding: left/right towards or away from the player once per change of half while passes remain; lip trick: random.
Start a swing: only for the pole holder, with fire newly pressed, no swing running ($33 = 0) and the cooldown over ($34 = 0): swing timer $33 = $20 (32 frames).
Once a frame: count the swing timer $33 down; when it reaches 0 start the 32-frame cooldown $34; count $34 down. A hit scores only while $33 runs, and $33 also flashes the pole colour.

The opponent-choice screen's loop (interrupts off, polled): opponent $35 from 1; each pass counts a frame, polls RUN/STOP, waits for the raster to wrap, shows sprite 0 (block $A0, the arrow at $E800) at X $20, Y from choice_arrow_y ($2FD4: $49, $8C, $CF) and a colour from choice_arrow_colours ($2FCC) cycled every 4 frames. Both joystick ports are read together ($DC00 AND $DC01); a newly pressed up moves to the previous face (not below 1), down to the next (not above 3), fire returns with the choice in $35.
RUN/STOP (CIA 1 port B bit 7, newly pressed, with row 7 selected by the load stub's $DC00 = $7F): abandon the event, $FE12 = $FF and end_event.
Commodore key (port B bit 5, newly pressed): flip the music flag $FE10 and copy it to music_off_request $42; music off makes the main loop silence the driver, music on queues sound 1 again.

End the joust: reset the sound driver and JMP $FE06 (event_done in the resident event manager). Reached when a match is decided and both skaters are back on the deck (set_state $17D2), and from RUN/STOP.
Queue sound ID A in the game's 16-byte ring (sound_ring $2FDA, write index $C3); the main loop passes it to queue_sound_id. No overflow check.
Take the next sound ID from the ring (read index $C4).

Unpack run-length data from ($12) to ($14) until $12/$13 reaches the end address in $16/$17: a control byte $00-$7F copies the next n+1 bytes, $80-$FF repeats the next byte n - $7F times (X counts down from n to $7F). Same code as High Jump's $1B6A.

156 bytes ($2190-$222B) between unpack_rle and the sound driver's variables: a $00/$FF stripe pattern like uninitialised memory (with $F7, $40 and $7F bytes mixed in), saved as part of file $14. No instruction reads or writes it; High Jump has a gap of the same size before its sound variables ($217F-$221A).

Number of sound IDs waiting in pending_sound_ids ($2288), 0-16. queue_sound_id ($2306) appends while it is below $10 (a 17th request is dropped); update_sid_voices ($233D) drains it to zero each tick. Cleared with the rest of $222C-$2297 by init_sound_driver.

Lowest priority among the three slots (the one a new sound must equal or beat). Recomputed at $29CD-$29E6 after each start; set to 0 when a slot finishes ($2932), so the next request always wins that free slot.
Slot offset (0, 2 or 4) of the slot holding sound_weakest_priority: where start_sound_on_weakest_slot ($2992) puts the next accepted sound. Set at $29E9 and, when a slot ends, at $2935.
The primary-script command byte being executed, saved by dispatch_sound_opcode ($23A7). Handlers test its bit 7 (BIT $222F) for the operand mode and op 7 re-reads its high nibble.
Low byte of the left-hand value for sound op 6 (compare): the slot's frequency, pulse width, sustain level, loop counter or a byte read from memory; $2231 holds the high byte for 16-bit compares.
High byte of the 16-bit left-hand compare value (frequency or pulse width) for sound op 6, compared first at $26BE.
Low byte (or only byte) of the right-hand operand of sound op 6, fetched by $26DA/$26ED from the script or through an address.
High byte of the right-hand operand for 16-bit compares in sound op 6 (set by $26ED).
Per-slot shadow of the SID frequency low byte, at $2234/$2236/$2238 for slot offsets 0/2/4 (voices 3/2/1). Written with every frequency change and read back by op 4 (add) and op 6 (compare).
Per-slot shadow of the SID frequency high byte, at $2235/$2237/$2239 for slot offsets 0/2/4; paired with slot_freq_lo.
Per-slot shadow of the SID pulse-width low byte, at $223A/$223C/$223E for slot offsets 0/2/4; set by op 1 and note command $AD, added to by op 4, compared by op 6.
Per-slot shadow of the SID pulse-width high nibble, at $223B/$223D/$223F for slot offsets 0/2/4.
Low byte of slot 0's call-stack base address (init_sound_driver stores $2298); the three slots' base pointers are words at $2240, $2242, $2244, read as $2240,x at $2619 and $2939.
High byte of slot 0's call-stack base ($22), read as $2241,x with the low byte at $2240,x.
Low byte of slot 2's (SID voice 2's) call-stack base: init_sound_driver stores $97, so slot 2 nests at $22A8.
High byte of slot 2's call-stack base ($22).
Low byte of slot 4's (SID voice 1's) call-stack base: init_sound_driver stores $A7, so slot 4 nests at $22B8.
High byte of slot 4's call-stack base ($22).

Four note durations per slot, $2246-$2249 (slot 0), $224A-$224D (slot 2), $224E-$2251 (slot 4), indexed by slot*2 + bits 7-6 of a note byte. The chosen value goes to the slot's wait timer ($225E,x). Loaded by op $97 and note command $5D.

Four gate lengths per slot, $2252-$2255, $2256-$2259, $225A-$225D, chosen like slot_note_durations. Non-zero: the note sets the gate bit and the gate timer ($225F,x); zero: the note changes pitch without re-gating. Loaded by op $A7 and note command $6D.

Per-slot wait timer at $225E/$2260/$2262 (slot offsets 0/2/4): while non-zero update_sid_voices decrements it instead of reading the script; a value N set in one tick makes the slot read again N+1 ticks later (checked against SID writes in the simulator). Set by op 8, notes and note commands.

Per-slot gate timer at $225F/$2261/$2263: when flag bit 5 is set it counts down each tick and, G+1 ticks after a value G was set, clears the gate bit (bit 0) of the voice's control register ($236E), starting the release. The shadow $226B,x keeps the gate bit.
Sound ID playing in each slot, at $2264/$2266/$2268; 0 after the slot ends. stop_sound ($2314) searches it.
Per-slot flags at $2265/$2267/$2269: 0 idle; bit 6 active (set to $40 at start); bit 5 gate timer running; bit 4 inside a script call (call stack non-empty); bit 7 paused (skipped by the updater).
Per-slot sustain level counter (low nibble used) at $226A/$226C/$226E: op $24 adds to it and writes it as the high nibble of the SID sustain/release register; op $26 compares it.

Per-slot shadow of the SID control register (waveform bits and gate) at $226B/$226D/$226F; notes set bit 0 in it ($274F); the gate timer writes it to the SID with bit 0 clear ($236E) and leaves the shadow as it is.
Per-slot loop counter at $2270/$2272/$2274: set by op $31, added to by op $34, compared by op $36, and decremented by the loop op $15 (jump while non-zero).

Priority of the sound in slot 0 (SID voice 3); the slots' priorities are at $2271/$2273/$2275. Set from sound_priorities ($321E) on start, cleared at end; compared at $29CD-$29E6 to find the weakest slot.
Priority of the sound in slot 2 (SID voice 2), read directly at $29D2/$29D9 when finding the weakest slot.
Priority of the sound in slot 4 (SID voice 1), read directly at $29CF when finding the weakest slot (slot 4 is the first candidate).
Per-slot shadow of the SID attack/decay register at $2276/$2278/$227A; set by op $41 and note command $8D.
Per-slot shadow of the SID sustain/release register at $2277/$2279/$227B; op $24 rewrites its high nibble from slot_sustain_level.

Bytes used on each slot's call stack at $227C/$227E/$2280 (two per nested call); a call pushes the return pointer at stack base + depth, a return pops it. Not range-checked: more than 8 nested calls would run into the next slot's stack.
Result of the slot's last op 6 compare at $227D/$227F/$2281, as the processor's C and Z bits: 0 less, 1 greater, 3 equal. Tested by the conditional jumps of op 5 against $2646/$264C.

Per-slot octave shift at $2282/$2284/$2286: the number of right shifts applied to note frequencies before the note's own octave bits are added (note_frequency, $28F4). Set by op $B7 and note command $4D.
Sixteen-byte queue of requested sound IDs: queue_sound_id ($2306) appends while sound_pending_count is below $10; update_sid_voices starts them newest first and empties the queue each tick.

Three 16-byte call stacks for nested sound scripts, $2298 (slot 0), $22A8 (slot 2), $22B8 (slot 4), addressed through slot_stack_ptr_lo/hi. Each call pushes a two-byte return address. Not cleared by init: the bytes here are whatever the file carried; 8 levels per slot.

Sound driver reset: zero the script pointers $02-$07 and all driver state $222C-$2297, silence the three SID control registers, set volume $0F with no filter ($D418), and point the slots' call stacks at $2298/$22A8/$22B8. Called by joust_restart ($0858), by the main loop when music_off_request is set ($0882) and by end_event ($2145). The driver ($22C8-$29EC) is High Jump's ($22B7-$29DB) byte for byte, $11 bytes higher, except the addresses of the sound tables ($31EA, $3204, $321E).

Request sound ID A: append it to pending_sound_ids unless 16 are already waiting (then the request is silently dropped). Called from the main loop ($0892, IDs taken from the game's sound ring at $2FDA) and by sound op 2 ($24AA). Clobbers X.

Stop sound ID A wherever it plays: search slot_sound_id for slots 4, 2, 0 and, if found, silence that slot through $2921 with interrupts disabled. No caller in the Pool Joust either (no JSR or JMP to it in memory); part of the shared driver.
Found: Y = the slot's SID register offset; silence the slot with IRQs masked.

Set slot A (0-2, doubled to the slot offset) to flags $80 so update_sid_voices skips it. It replaces all flags rather than setting bit 7. No caller in the Pool Joust either (byte scan of memory for JSR/JMP).
Clear bit 7 of slot A's flags. After pause_sound_slot the flags are $80, so this leaves 0 (idle) and the slot does not resume. No caller in the Pool Joust either (byte scan of memory for JSR/JMP).

One sound tick (run by the main loop once for each raster frame the interrupt counts in sound_ticks $C5): start every queued ID (start_sound_on_weakest_slot), then for slots 4, 2, 0 (SID voices 1, 2, 3): skip if idle or paused; run the gate timer; if the wait timer is zero, execute script commands until a $00 byte (end of tick) or the slot ends.
Read the next byte of slot X's primary script through ($02,X) and advance the pointer; the Z flag reflects the byte (a $00 byte ends the tick at $238B).

Execute primary command A: save it in sound_command_byte, push the handler for its low nibble from $23BF/$23CF (RTS trick), and enter it with A = high nibble. Bit 7 of the command is the operand-mode flag; bits 6-4 select the sub-operation.

High bytes of the 16 primary sound-op handlers minus one, indexed by the low nibble of the command: 0 end/return ($291A), 1 set register ($23DF), 2 queue sound ($24A3), 3 poke/wait ($24B2), 4 add ($251D), 5 jump/loop/call ($25AC), 6 compare ($2652), 7 note stream ($270B), 8 wait ($2902), 9 end, A call 6502 code ($2962), B-F end.
Low bytes of the 16 primary sound-op handlers minus one (paired with $23BF); RTS lands one byte higher, on the handler.

Op $x1, set a voice register, sub-op = bits 6-4: 0 frequency (2 bytes lo,hi), 1-2 pulse width (2), 3 loop counter (1), 4 attack/decay (1), 5 sustain/release (1), 6-7 control/waveform (1). Bit 7 clear: the value follows in the script; bit 7 set: a 2-byte address follows and the value is read from there. Writes the SID and the slot shadow.
Op $02: the next script byte is a sound ID to request through queue_sound_id (started at the next tick, by priority); X and Y preserved.

Op 3 with an address operand (2 bytes). Sub-op 1 ($13/$93), wait-until: compare memory at the address with a value (bit 7 set: a literal byte; clear: a byte read through a second address); if unequal, back the script up 4 bytes and end this slot's tick, so it retries next tick. Other sub-ops ($03/$83), poke: store a value there (bit 7 clear: literal; set: read through a second address).

Unequal: rewind the script by 4 (right for the literal form $93 aa aa vv; the address form is 5 bytes long, so it would resume on its second byte), drop the dispatcher's return and go to the next slot.

Op 4, add to a register, sub-op = bits 6-4: 0 frequency += 2-byte value (bit 7 set: value read through an address), 1 pulse width += 2 bytes, 2 sustain level += byte, rewrite sustain/release and set the gate bit (re-trigger), 3+ loop counter += byte. Writes the SID and the shadows; 16-bit adds wrap.

Op 5, script flow. Bit 7 clear: $05 jump to a 2-byte address; $15 decrement the loop counter, jump while non-zero, else skip the address; $25 call (push the return pointer on the slot's stack, set flag bit 4); $35 replace this slot's sound with the ID in the next byte; others end. Bit 7 set: conditional jump on the last compare, $85 equal, $95 less, $A5 not equal, $B5 greater, $C5 less or equal, $D5 greater or equal; $E5/$F5 end.
First accepted compare result for the conditional jumps $85-$D5 (index = bits 6-4): 3,0,1,1,0,1. A jump is taken when slot_compare_result equals this byte or the one at $264C.
Second accepted compare result for the conditional jumps (same index): 3,0,0,1,3,3. With $2646 this gives equal, less, not equal (1 or 0), greater, less-or-equal (0 or 3), greater-or-equal (1 or 3).

Op 6, compare and keep the result in slot_compare_result, sub-op = bits 6-4: 0 frequency vs 2-byte operand, 1 pulse width vs 2 bytes, 2 sustain level vs byte, 3 loop counter vs byte, 7 the byte at a 2-byte address vs byte; others end the script. Bit 7 set: the operand is read through an address instead.
Bytes 2C A9 01: BIT $01A9 hides LDA #$01 at $26D4, the entry for 'greater' (result 1); entered at $26D3 it gives 0, 'less'.
Fetch op 6's one-byte right operand into sound_compare_right: the next script byte, or (command bit 7 set) the byte read through a 2-byte address.
Fetch op 6's two-byte right operand into sound_compare_right/_hi: two script bytes, or (command bit 7 set) the word read through a 2-byte address.

Op 7. Bit 7 clear ($07): play the next event of the slot's note stream at ($08,X): low nibble 0-C a note (frequency table index, 0 silent), bits 5-4 extra octave shift, bits 7-6 pick duration and gate length; $xD a note command (handler $27FE by high nibble, next byte its argument); $0E call a primary-script subroutine at the next 2 bytes; else end. Bit 7 set: $87 set the stream pointer, $97 four durations, $A7 four gate lengths, $B7 octave shift.
Read the next byte of slot X's note stream through ($08,X) and advance that pointer.

Low bytes of the 11 note-stream command handlers, indexed by the high nibble of a $xD stream byte: 0 note+duration, 1 frequency+duration, 2 note+duration+gate, 3 frequency+duration+gate, 4 octave shift, 5 durations, 6 gate lengths, 7 control, 8 attack/decay, 9 sustain/release, A pulse width. $BD-$FD index past the table (no check).
High bytes of the 11 note-stream command handlers, paired with note_command_handlers_lo; read at $2768 and jumped to through $0E/$0F.
Note command $0D: the argument is a note byte (low nibble note, bits 5-4 octave); the next stream byte is a literal duration for the wait timer. Sets the frequency without touching the gate.
Note command $1D: the argument and the next byte are a literal SID frequency (low, high); the next byte is the duration. No gate change.
Note command $2D: note byte argument, then a literal duration and gate length; starts the gate timer (flag bit 5) but does not set the gate bit itself.
Note command $3D: literal frequency (argument = low, next = high), then duration and gate length; starts the gate timer without setting the gate bit.
Note command $4D: the argument becomes the slot's octave shift ($2282,x); then the next stream event is played in the same tick.
Note command $5D: the argument and the next three stream bytes replace the slot's four note durations ($2246); then the next event is played.
Note command $6D: the argument and the next three stream bytes replace the slot's four gate lengths ($2252); then the next event is played.
Note command $7D: write the argument to the voice's SID control register (waveform, gate) and its shadow, then play the next event.
Note command $8D: write the argument to the voice's attack/decay register and shadow, then play the next event.
Note command $9D: write the argument to the voice's sustain/release register and shadow, then play the next event.
Note command $AD: the argument and the next stream byte are the pulse width (low, high), written to the SID and shadows; then the next event is played.

Note number A (0-15) to frequency in $0E/$0F: read the top-octave value from note_freq_lo/hi and shift it right by (bits 5-4 of the note byte in $11) + the slot's octave shift. Used by notes and note commands $0D/$2D.

Op 8: the next byte is a wait. $08 N: set the slot's wait timer, so the script resumes N+1 ticks later (once a $00 has ended this tick). $88 G: set the gate timer instead and flag bit 5, so the gate is released G+1 ticks later while the script runs on.
Op 0/9/B-F (and every invalid sub-op): if the slot is inside a call (flag bit 4), pop the return pointer from its call stack and continue there; otherwise fall into silence_sound_slot.

End slot X: clear the voice's control register (gate off, no waveform), the slot's ID, flags, stack depth and priority, and make it the weakest slot (priority 0) for the next request. Y = the voice's SID register offset. Also called from stop_sound.

Op $0A: call the 6502 routine at the 2-byte address that follows, preserving X and Y. The music's two scripts use it to call $33FF and $3418, which choose the next phrase; sound 14 calls $32C1 and $32D6; sound 25 would call $CD00.
JMP ($000E): the indirect call made by sound_opA_call_code; returns to $2973 when the called routine executes RTS.

Read a 2-byte address from slot X's script and return the byte there in A and the following byte in $11 (a little-endian word), with Y restored to the voice's SID register offset. The operand form used when a command's bit 7 selects it.

Start sound ID A if its priority (sound_priorities, $321E) is at least sound_weakest_priority: replace the sound in slot sound_weakest_slot. Equal priority wins, so a new sound replaces an old one of the same rank.

Start sound ID Y with priority A on slot X: set the slot's priority and ID, its script pointer from sound_script_addresses ($31EA/$3204), clear its timers and stack, set flags $40, zero the voice's seven SID registers, then find the new weakest slot (slot 4 first, then 2, then 0) for sound_weakest_priority/slot. Also used by op $35.

SID register offset of each sound slot, read at even X only: $29ED (slot 0) $0E = voice 3, $29EF (slot 2) $07 = voice 2, $29F1 (slot 4) $00 = voice 1. The odd bytes $29EE/$29F0 are never read as offsets.

Low bytes of the note frequency table, 16 entries indexed by the note's low nibble: 0 silence ($0000), 1-12 the twelve semitones A, A#, B, C ... G# of the top octave ($70C7 ... $D4E6), 13-15 zero. In NTSC SID units entry 1 is 1760 Hz (A6); on a PAL machine it plays about 0.65 semitone flat.

High bytes of the note frequency table ($00,$70,$77,$7E,$86,$8E,$96,$9F,$A8,$B3,$BD,$C8,$D4,0,0,0); each step is a factor of about 1.0595, one semitone. note_frequency shifts the value right once per octave down.
Raster band handlers, read at $0B93/$0B99 by band number $1E: band 0 band0_status_irq ($0BB6), band 1 band1_play_irq ($0D8B).
High bytes of raster_handlers, read at $0B99 (LDA $2A13,X) for the JSR at $0B9F.
Raster compare line per band: $FB (band 0, below the picture) and $38 (band 1, just above the multicolour picture). Read by install_raster_irq and next_raster_band.
Next band after each band: 1, 0.

Pose at the top band of the wall (path Y $96-$B9) by queued trick $5E (0-3): $00, $16, $00, $35; lean_poses_back ($2A1E: $08, $1B, $08, $35) when riding backwards; the pole holder's sets are lean_poses_pole ($2A22: $41, $58, $41, $6E) and $2A26 ($49, $5D, $49, $6E). Read by state02_riding ($0FAA-$0FC2); $2A1A's first byte is also the knocked-off board's pose ($1018).
Riding backwards: $08, $1B, $08, $35 (see lean_poses).
The pole holder's lean poses: $41, $58, $41, $6E; backwards $2A26: $49, $5D, $49, $6E.
The pole holder riding backwards: $49, $5D, $49, $6E.
State entered at the top of a wall by queued trick $5E: 0 -> 4 (air turn), 1 -> 6 (lip trick), 2 -> $0E (slide turn), 3 -> $12 (climb out). Read at $0FED.
Per trick $5E: non-zero holds the path Y at $96 in move_skater ($130C): 0, 1, 1, 1, so only the air turn leaves the coping.
Values choose_trick stores in $5E: $2A32 = 0 (no input: air turn), $2A33 = 2 ($5C: slide turn), $2A34 = 1 ($5D: lip trick).
choose_trick reads this byte at $19E7: 2, the slide turn, given for a left/right press stored in $5C.
choose_trick reads this byte at $19F1: 1, the lip trick, for a press stored in $5D.

Five 3-byte rows for state02_riding: a path-Y threshold, then the pose for riding forwards and for riding backwards. Thresholds $BA, $D6, $E3, $EC, $FF: the row is the first whose threshold exceeds the skater's path Y. Row 0's poses ($FF) mean 'use lean_poses'. This set is used when the facing and the speed's sign differ (descending); riding_pose_rows_up ($2A44) when they agree. Poses $20-$27 lean the skater with the slope.
riding_pose_rows from its second column: state0A_knocked_off reads the board pose here at $1013 (LDA $2A36,Y), the forward-riding pose of the row chosen by height.
The same rows for the other direction of travel: thresholds as riding_pose_rows, poses $28-$2B and $24-$27.
Five poses of the lip trick (states 6 and 8, the latter backwards): $16-$1A; lip_trick_poses_back ($2A58: $1B-$1F) when riding backwards.
Lip trick riding backwards: $1B-$1F.

Four 8-pose sequences of the lip turn (state $0C), by riding backwards $51 and turn direction $5A: forwards $2A5D (1A 19 18 17 00 02 04 06) and $2A65 (1A 19 18 17 00 0E 0C 0A), backwards $2A6D and $2A75; the last four of each are spin poses (0-$0F), the first four the lip poses run backwards.
Lip turn, forwards, other direction.
Lip turn, backwards: 1F 1E 1D 1C 08 0A 0C 0E.
Lip turn, backwards, other direction: 1F 1E 1D 1C 08 06 04 02.
Eight drop-in poses (state 0): $10, $10, $11-$15, $00; its first entry is also the starting pose (setup_joust). drop_in_poses_pole ($2A85: $51-$57, $41) for the pole holder.
The pole holder's drop-in poses: $51-$57, $41.
Nine poses of the slide turn (state $0E): spin poses $00, $0F down to $08, read backwards when riding backwards; holder +$41.
Four flying-body poses of a knocked-off skater, $3A-$3D, cycled while in the air (state $0A).
Three 7-pose tumbles after the body lands, chosen at random ($62, via knock_tumble_ptrs $2AAF): $2A9A (3E 3F 3F 40 40 40 3F), $2AA1 (78 78 79 7A 7A 7A 7A), $2AA8 ($7B seven times).
Addresses of the three tumbles: $2A9A, $2AA1, $2AA8.
High bytes of knock_tumble_ptrs, read at $107E (LDA $2AB0,Y).
Four climb-out poses (state $12): $6E-$71; the same again at $2AB9 for riding backwards.
Climb-out poses when riding backwards: $6E-$71 (identical).
Thirteen poses of state $14, standing on the deck after climbing out: $72-$76 twice, then $72-$74; the handler steps through 12.
Fidget a ($5A = 0): poses indexed by animation step: $10 then $2D-$34 and back to $10 (19 entries).
Fidget b ($5A = 1): $10/$11 alternating, then $10 (10 entries).
Steps in each fidget: $13 (19) for a, $0A (10) for b.

Handler of each skater state, indexed by the state number (even, 0-$14) at $0E4F: 0 deck $0E61, 2 riding $0F57, 4 air turn $10E2, 6 lip trick $1111, 8 lip return $1181, $0A knocked off $0FF3, $0C lip turn $11BB, $0E slide turn $121A, $10 fidget $0EF9, $12 climb out $1263, $14 waiting $1295.
High bytes of state_handlers, read at $0E55 (LDA $2AEA,Y) for the JSR at $0E5B.

The skater path: 273 entries of two bytes (X, Y), indexed by position (0-$110; positions $111-$222 read it mirrored) in lookup_path_xy ($146D): X stays 42 for entries 0-108 while Y rises one per entry from 64 (above the coping: air), then the curve of the wall to the flat bottom at Y 240 and the centre at X 182. Entry $56 is the coping (Y 150). Byte for byte High Jump's ramp profile ($2ACB-$2CEE). Entries 0-31.
path_profile continued (entries 32-63, Y 96-127 on the vertical part).
path_profile continued (entries 64-95; the coping, entry $56, is at $2BAB).
path_profile continued (entries 96-127: the vertical part ends at entry 108 and the wall starts to curve).
path_profile continued (entries 128-159).
path_profile continued (entries 160-191, reaching the flat Y 236-237).
path_profile continued (entries 192-223, Y 238-240).
path_profile continued (entries 224-255, the flat at Y 240).
path_profile, entries 256-272 ($2CFF-$2D22): the flat at Y 240, X 165-182, the last entry the centre of the pool.
Sixteen digit characters 0-9, A-F (ASCII), read only by the unreferenced hex printer at $13E3. Same bytes as High Jump's $2CEF.

Five multicolour sprites ($2D33-$2E72), boxed digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, copied by setup_joust to $6A00-$6B3F (blocks $A8-$AC) and shown as the pass counter (block $A8 + passes left). Each is 63 bytes plus a pad byte.
Pass counter sprite 2 (copied to $6A40).
Pass counter sprite 3 (copied to $6A80).
Pass counter sprite 4 (copied to $6AC0).
Pass counter sprite 5 (copied to $6B00).
Hires sprite of the arrow on the opponent-choice screen, 63 bytes, copied to $E800 (block $A0 of bank 3) by show_choice_screen.
Byte after the arrow sprite's 63 bytes: show_choice_screen copies only offsets $00-$3E ($0B11), and nothing else reads it.

Sprite colours for skater_sprite_colours: first skater $2EB3-$2EB6 (pole, then three body parts; $2EB6 is set from the slot's $FE02), second skater $2EB7-$2EBA (pole, then $2EB8-$2EBA from setup_opponent). The two pole colours are rewritten every frame from pole_flash_colours. $2EBB-$2EC2 (01 01 07 07 03 03 0A 0A) are never read.
First skater's third body sprite colour, overwritten from the event manager's slot attribute $FE02 by setup_joust at $0A00 ($05 in the play snapshot, which is taken before setup_joust runs).

Second skater's pole colour, rewritten every frame by setup_sprites ($0BF4) with the same pole_flash_colours entry as $2EB3; then the second skater's body colours $2EB8-$2EBA, set by setup_opponent ($1D01, $1D07, $1D12).

Second skater's three body colours, written by setup_opponent from opponent_colour_1/2/3 ($1D01, $1D07, $1D12; with two humans the third comes from the slot's $FE0B); then $2EBB-$2EC2 (01 01 07 07 03 03 0A 0A), which nothing reads.
Second skater's second body colour, written at $1D07 from opponent_colour_2 ($2F71).
Second skater's third body colour, written at $1D12 from opponent_colour_3 ($2F75), or from the slot's $FE0B with two humans; then $2EBB-$2EC2 (01 01 07 07 03 03 0A 0A), never read.
Pass counter sprite position by pole holder (0 first skater, 1 second): X low $2EC3/$2EC4 = $38/$20, X high bit $2EC5/$2EC6 = 1/0 (so X = $138 or $20), Y $2EC7/$2EC8 = $52.
pass_counter_pos X high bits (1 for the first skater as holder, 0 for the second), read at $0D80; then the Y bytes $2EC7/$2EC8, both $52.
pass_counter_pos Y for either holder: $52, $52 (read at $0D6B).
Forty colour bytes for text row 0 (ink in the high nibble, paper in the low): 16 cyan-on-blue, 24 white-on-blue, used for the name and the PRESS YOUR BUTTON prompt.
The prompt's other flash colours: 16 cyan, 24 yellow on blue.
Status row colours from the VS step on: white for the score fields (3 cells at each end), cyan for the names, white for the 'VS'.
The computer opponents' names, zero-terminated: POSEUR PETE ($2F41), AGGRO' EDDIE ($2F4D), LESTER ($2F5A).
AGGRO' EDDIE, zero-terminated; opponent_names entry 2 points here ($2F65).
LESTER, zero-terminated; opponent_names entry 3 points here.
Name pointer per opponent choice $35 (0-3): 0 unused ($0000; two humans use the slot's name), then $2F41, $2F4D, $2F5A.
